newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to set up privatisation agency soon.
newsitem.headline: Poland to set up privatisation agency soon.

text.p: The Polish government is likely to approve regulations on Tuesday needed to set up a privatisation agency, as envisaged by the ongoing reorganisation of ministries, the government spokeswoman said.
Aleksandra Jakubowska told a news briefing that the prime minister would then appoint the head of the agency.
"I expect that the prime minister will promptly nominate the agency's head," she said.
The agency, due to supervise technicalities of privatisation, is envisaged by the cabinet reform under which the privatisation ministry was replaced last year by a more powerful treasury ministry.

During the reform, the liberal Privatisation Minister Wieslaw Kaczamrek became the economy minister and the supervision over sell-offs fell in the hands of Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz, known for his cautious attitude to privatisation.
Jakubowska said that proposing a candidate to head the agency would be up to Pietrewicz, but the final decision on the appointnment rested with the prime minister.

The agency is to oversee flotations of state-owned enterprises and their sales to strategic investors, except for largest, strategic projects, which will be supervised by the treasury ministry itself.
More than 40 privatisation projects, currently run by the treasury ministry, would be completed by the ministry.
